intrebari.intrebare: On St Brice's Day, 13 November 1002, King Æthelred the Unready ordered the killing of which people living in England?
intrebari.explicatie: The St Brice's Day massacre (1002) targeted Danish settlers in England.

intrebari.intrebare: Queen Eleanor of Castile died on 28 November 1290. Her grieving husband, Edward I, built a series of monuments in her memory known as...
intrebari.explicatie: Twelve Eleanor crosses marked the places where her body rested on the way to London; Charing Cross is named after the last one.

intrebari.intrebare: Which powerful chancellor of Henry VIII died at Leicester on 29 November 1530 while travelling to face charges of treason?
intrebari.explicatie: Wolsey died at Leicester Abbey in November 1530. Cromwell and More were executed; Cranmer was burned at the stake.

intrebari.intrebare: The Act of Supremacy, passed by Parliament in November 1534, declared Henry VIII...
variante: Supreme Head of the Church of England
intrebari.explicatie: The 1534 Act made the king head of the English Church, completing the break with Rome.

intrebari.intrebare: On 17 November 1558, Elizabeth I became queen after the death of which monarch?
intrebari.explicatie: Elizabeth succeeded her half-sister Mary I. 17 November was later celebrated as 'Accession Day'.

intrebari.intrebare: Which king, later executed in 1649, was born in Dunfermline, Scotland, on 19 November 1600?
intrebari.explicatie: Charles I was born in Dunfermline Palace on 19 November 1600.

intrebari.intrebare: What did Guy Fawkes and his fellow conspirators plan to blow up on 5 November 1605?
intrebari.explicatie: The Gunpowder Plot aimed to blow up the House of Lords during the State Opening of Parliament.

intrebari.intrebare: Which king was the main target of the Gunpowder Plot in 1605?
intrebari.explicatie: The Catholic plotters wanted to kill the Protestant King James I.

intrebari.intrebare: Where was Guy Fawkes discovered in the early hours of 5 November 1605?
variante: in a cellar beneath the House of Lords
intrebari.explicatie: He was caught guarding 36 barrels of gunpowder in a cellar (undercroft) below the House of Lords.

intrebari.intrebare: After the plot failed, Parliament passed a law in 1606 ordering people to mark 5 November every year as a day of...
intrebari.explicatie: The Observance of 5th November Act (1606) made the day a day of thanksgiving for the king's survival.

intrebari.intrebare: The Pilgrims who signed the Mayflower Compact in November 1620 had made their final departure from which English port?
intrebari.explicatie: The Mayflower left Plymouth in September 1620 and reached Cape Cod in November.

intrebari.intrebare: Which scientific society was founded in London on 28 November 1660?
intrebari.explicatie: The Royal Society was founded on 28 November 1660, after a lecture by Christopher Wren.

intrebari.intrebare: On 5 November 1688, William of Orange landed at Torbay in Devon, beginning what became known as the...
intrebari.explicatie: William's landing led to the flight of James II and the 'Glorious Revolution'.

intrebari.intrebare: News of which naval victory, and of Admiral Nelson's death, reached London on 6 November 1805?
intrebari.explicatie: Trafalgar was fought on 21 October 1805; the news reached the Admiralty on 6 November.

intrebari.intrebare: Which son of Queen Victoria, later king, was born on 9 November 1841?
intrebari.explicatie: Albert Edward, the future Edward VII, was born at Buckingham Palace on 9 November 1841.

intrebari.intrebare: In November 1854, which nurse arrived at the British army hospital in Scutari during the Crimean War?
intrebari.explicatie: Florence Nightingale arrived at Scutari in early November 1854 with a team of nurses.

intrebari.intrebare: Which famous book by Charles Darwin was first published on 24 November 1859?
intrebari.explicatie: 'On the Origin of Species' sold out on its first day of publication.

intrebari.intrebare: Which future Prime Minister was born at Blenheim Palace on 30 November 1874?
intrebari.explicatie: Winston Churchill was born at Blenheim Palace, Oxfordshire.

intrebari.intrebare: Which First World War poet was killed on 4 November 1918, just one week before the Armistice?
intrebari.explicatie: Owen's family received the news on Armistice Day. Sassoon and Graves survived the war; Brooke died in 1915.

intrebari.intrebare: At what time did the Armistice ending the fighting of the First World War take effect on 11 November 1918?
intrebari.explicatie: 'The eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month.'

intrebari.intrebare: An Act of Parliament passed in November 1918 allowed women in the UK to do what for the first time?
intrebari.explicatie: The Parliament (Qualification of Women) Act 1918 let women become MPs. Some women had won the vote earlier that year.

intrebari.intrebare: In November 1919, who was elected as the first woman to take her seat in the House of Commons?
intrebari.explicatie: Nancy Astor won Plymouth Sutton in November 1919. Markievicz had been elected in 1918 but did not take her seat.

intrebari.intrebare: Which war memorial in Whitehall was unveiled in its permanent stone form on 11 November 1920?
intrebari.explicatie: The Cenotaph, designed by Edwin Lutyens, is the focus of the national Remembrance ceremony.

intrebari.intrebare: On 11 November 1920, the body of which symbolic figure was buried in Westminster Abbey?
intrebari.explicatie: An unidentified soldier was buried to represent all those killed in the First World War.

intrebari.intrebare: On 4 November 1922, British archaeologist Howard Carter's team found the first step leading to the tomb of which pharaoh?
intrebari.explicatie: The discovery in Egypt's Valley of the Kings became world-famous.

intrebari.intrebare: Which broadcaster began daily radio broadcasts from London on 14 November 1922?
intrebari.explicatie: The British Broadcasting Company began daily broadcasts from station 2LO.

intrebari.intrebare: On 2 November 1936, the BBC began the world's first regular high-definition television service from which London building?
intrebari.explicatie: Alexandra Palace, in north London, is still known as 'the birthplace of television'.

intrebari.intrebare: Which city's medieval cathedral was destroyed in a German air raid on 14 November 1940?
intrebari.explicatie: The ruins of old Coventry Cathedral still stand beside the new cathedral.

intrebari.intrebare: On the night of 11–12 November 1940, aircraft from HMS Illustrious attacked the Italian fleet at which harbour?
intrebari.explicatie: The Battle of Taranto was the first all-aircraft naval attack in history.

intrebari.intrebare: After the victory at El Alamein, Churchill said on 10 November 1942: 'This is not the end... It is, perhaps, the end of the ______.'
intrebari.explicatie: 'Now this is not the end. It is not even the beginning of the end. But it is, perhaps, the end of the beginning.'

intrebari.intrebare: On 20 November 1947, Princess Elizabeth married Philip Mountbatten in which church?
intrebari.explicatie: The wedding at Westminster Abbey was broadcast on radio to 200 million people.

intrebari.intrebare: Which future king was born at Buckingham Palace on 14 November 1948?
intrebari.explicatie: Charles III was born on 14 November 1948 and became king in 2022.

intrebari.intrebare: Which Prime Minister announced her resignation on 22 November 1990?
intrebari.explicatie: Margaret Thatcher resigned after 11 years in office. Barbara Castle was a minister but never Prime Minister.

intrebari.intrebare: Which royal residence was badly damaged by fire on 20 November 1992?
intrebari.explicatie: The fire destroyed or damaged more than 100 rooms; restoration took five years.

intrebari.intrebare: In a speech in November 1992, Queen Elizabeth II described that year as her...
intrebari.explicatie: Latin for 'horrible year' — 1992 included the Windsor fire and several royal separations.

intrebari.intrebare: The Maastricht Treaty, which created the European Union, came into force on 1 November 1993. In which year did the UK leave the EU?
intrebari.explicatie: The UK voted to leave in 2016 and formally left on 31 January 2020.

intrebari.intrebare: In November 1994, regular passenger trains began running through which tunnel?
intrebari.explicatie: Eurostar services between London, Paris and Brussels began on 14 November 1994.

intrebari.intrebare: The first draw of which game took place on BBC television on 19 November 1994?
intrebari.explicatie: The first National Lottery draw was watched by millions; Premium Bonds date from 1956.

intrebari.intrebare: On 22 November 2003, England became the first northern-hemisphere team to win which tournament?
intrebari.explicatie: Jonny Wilkinson's drop goal in extra time beat Australia in Sydney.

intrebari.intrebare: Since 1919, how long is the silence held at 11 a.m. on Armistice Day?
intrebari.explicatie: King George V asked for a two-minute silence on the first anniversary of the Armistice in 1919.
